As the committee discussed increasing the threshold of CSR funding that requires independent oversight, certain members cited TNM ’s investigation, to highlight the need for auditing CSR funding and having independent directors on the CSR committee. The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes key changes to the CSR rules under the Companies Act, 2013, purportedly to reduce “compliance burden.” However, some members argued against reducing accountability for CSR expenditure, as it could result in misuse of funds. TNM reported in July that the ONGC, a state-owned company and one of India's largest public sector undertakings, gave Rs 668.01 crore of CSR funds to 20 registered organisations linked to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) over 10 years. items.title: You only appoint judges with your ideology: Menaka Guruswamy in Rajya Sabha debate on Supreme Court judges bill
items.summary: Trinamool Congress MP and Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy on Wednesday argued in the Rajya Sabha that the government was favouring candidates who shared its ideology while making judicial appointments. “You only appoint judges who you think have your ideology! ” she said. Deputy Chairman Harivansh Narayan Singh, however, immediately directed that the remark would not go on record. Guruswamy was speaking during the debate on the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 , which increases the sanctioned strength of the Court from 34 to 38 judges, including the CJI. After receiving assent in the Lok Sabha earlier this week, the Bill was passed in the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday. In her speech, she also spoke about women, religious minorities and members of the LGBTQ community remaining inadequately represented in the judiciary. The Senior Advocate highlighted the inadequate representation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in judicial appointments. items.title: Puzzled by law student's answers, Allahabad HC asks Law Commission to examine standards of legal education
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently asked the Law Commission of India to consider examining broader issues relating to the standards of legal education in India and prepare a report to suggest appropriate reforms. Justice Vinod Diwakar said legal education constitutes the foundation of the justice delivery system and any substantial decline in academic standards at the institutional level affects not merely the legal profession but the administration of justice itself. "Law Commission of India may consider examining the broader questions relating to the standards of legal education in the country, and may prepare a report thereon should it consider such a course appropriate," the Court said on July 17. The Court also asked the Bar Council of India (BCI) to consider whether the standards of legal education are commensurate with the object for which they are prescribed. It also asked BCI to examine whether the existing mechanism for the grant of approval to institutions imparting legal education requires strengthening to compete with globally competitive legal education standards. items.title: Delhi HC asks why Delhi Police didn't arrest man who impersonated judge, civil servant
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday denied anticipatory bail to a man accused of posing as a Patna High Court judge and a civil servant to obtain sensitive and confidential information from various senior authorities. Justice Girish Kathpalia noted with surprise that there were nearly a dozen FIRs against accused Manoj Kumar Jha and despite his anticipatory bail being rejected several times, including by the Supreme Court, the police was yet to arrest him. The Court said that this “conveys an impression that accused is being helped and there is something more that meets the eye”. “That being so, copy of this order be sent to the concerned Deputy Commissioner of Police through the learned Senior Standing Counsel for information and necessary action,” the Court ordered. items.title: Can there be blanket ban on disclosure of personal information? Supreme Court on challenge to RTI amendment
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday observed that a careful balance would have to be struck between citizens' right to information and the fundamental right to privacy while examining changes made to the Right to Information (RTI) Act through the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing petitions challenging the amendment to Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by which the public interest clause for disclosure of personal information was removed. The Court said the central constitutional issue before the Court was whether there can be a blanket prohibition on disclosure of personal information. "The question is whether there can be a blanket prohibition on disclosure of all digital personal information, or whether the legislation has to adopt a proportionate approach," said Justice Bagchi. He further said the Court would have to examine whether parliament's approach of expanding protection for personal information under the amended law satisfies constitutional standards. items.title: Is prior sanction needed to prosecute ex-civil servants for offences before 2018 amendment to PC Act? Delhi HC answers
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday ruled that the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act) - which extends the requirement for prior sanction to prosecute former civil servants - will apply retrospectively if the court has not already taken cognisance of the offence. A Division Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja said that if the Court has taken cognisance of the offence before the date on which the amendment came into effect - July 26, 2018 - there is no fresh requirement of prior sanction. “The relevant date for the application of the amended Section 19(1) of the 1988 Act is with effect from 26.07.2018. The Amendment Act, as far as amendment to Section 19(1) of the 1988 Act, is retrospective to the extent that the benefit thereunder would enure even where the offence is alleged to have been committed prior to its coming into force, however, it is prospective to the effect that, where cognizance of such offence already stands taken before 26.07.2018, the same shall not be reopened and there would be no fresh requirement of prior sanction in such cases. items.title: We are creating organised urban slums: Punjab & Haryana HC on faulty town planning
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Thursday remarked that authorities were creating "organised urban slums" in the country by regularising illegal constructions and allowing additional floor area for building constructions on the payment of charges. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor made the observation while questioning the concept of purchasable floor area ratio (FAR) in Haryana. Purchasable FAR is the extra floor area that a developer or property owner in Haryana can build by paying an additional fee to the government, over and above the normal FAR permitted under building regulations. The Court was hearing a batch of petitions related to alleged illegal constructions in DLF City, Gurugram. It noted that since governments regularly increase the FAR, townships were getting converted into slums. It added that the sole objective seems to be the generation of some revenue. items.title: Actress assault in van: Kerala High Court refuses to suspend jail sentence of vehicle driver
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently refused to suspend the jail sentence of Martin Antony, who was the driver of the vehicle in which a Malayalam cine actress was abducted and raped in 2017 [ Martin Antony v. State of Kerala ] . Antony had moved the High Court with an appeal against his conviction by a Sessions Court. He had also moved an application seeking to suspend the 20-year jail sentence imposed on him by the Sessions Court until his appeal before the High Court is decided. However, a Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan V and KV Jayakumar did not find merit in Antony's contention that he was merely the driver of the vehicle with no knowledge of the criminal conspiracy hatched to abduct and rape the actress. The Court, therefore, dismissed his plea for the suspension of his jail sentence. " We are unable to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the applicant that he was only a mere driver in the MO9 vehicle, with no active role in the commission of the crime or motive. items.title: Why don't you shut down Jantar Mantar protest site? Delhi High Court to Centre
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday asked the government why it was not considering shutting down Jantar Mantar area as a venue/ site for protests. Justice Amit Mahajan said that the city should not be held to ransom unnecessarily by such protests in the middle of the city. “Why don’t you shut it down? Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court Justice Mahajan made the remarks while hearing a plea filed by All India Dalit Christian Rights Protection Committee seeking directions to the Delhi Police to decide its plea seeking permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. Senior Advocate Sanjoy Ghose appeared for the petitioner and told the Bench that the Police has neither rejected the request nor allowed it. "We are saying maximum 75 people will come. They [Delhi Police] are sitting on our application since July. They have not rejected it," Ghose submitted. items.title: Verdict convicting M Geethanandan, others in Muthanga land agitation case needs scrutiny: Kerala HC
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday observed that the conviction of four persons in a case arising from the 2003 Muthanga land struggle will require thorough scrutiny. Justice A Badharudeen made the observation after noting that the trial court's finding on the applicability of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B of the IPC was only prima facie in nature, and not conclusive. The Court was hearing appeals filed by activist M Geethanandan, and Rameshan, Binu and Anilkumar who were convicted by a sessions court over the violent confrontation between police and adivasi protesters at Muthanga in 2003. "The judgment needs to be scrutinised because the sessions judge made only a prima facie finding on the evidence... It should have been a conclusive finding. This judgment must be scrutinised thoroughly," the Court said in its order. The Muthanga land struggle stemmed from an eviction drive carried out by the Kerala Police at the Muthanga Wildlife Sanctuary in Wayanad in 2003. The eviction drive led to a violent confrontation between the police and Adivasi protesters, which escalated into police firing. Five protesters and police constable KV Vinod died in the incident. Mishra's counsel today told the Court that the bail terms imposed on him, which included travel restrictions, prevented him from attending family functions, including his daughter's birthday celebrations. items.title: Former CAM Disputes Partner Shaneen Parikh joins Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas as a Partner
items.summary: Former Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Head of International Arbitration Shaneen Parikh has joined Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co as a Partner in its Dispute Resolution practice, specialising in International Arbitration. She will be based in Mumbai and takes up her role on August 17, 2026. Bar and Bench had covered Parikh's exit from CAM earlier this year. With over three decades of experience, Parikh is a dual-qualified solicitor in India and in England & Wales. She is an Advocate-on-Record at the Supreme Court of India and a registered foreign lawyer of the Singapore International Commercial Court. Parikh has acted in arbitrations seated in Singapore, London, New York, Geneva, Zurich, Dubai and across India, administered under the SIAC, ICC, LCIA, MCIA, DIAC and ICA Rules, as well as in ad hoc proceedings. Her work covers both commercial and investor-state disputes, and spans shareholder and post M&A disputes, private equity exits, put options and valuations, ISDA and structured financial products, infrastructure and construction, and media and intellectual property. items.title: How teens with PMOS are made to live with shame, fear and isolation
items.summary: During her high school, while most teenagers were worrying about classes, friendships and future plans, Nitha (name changed) stopped taking photos of herself altogether. Her body was changing in ways she could not understand. She experienced unexplained weight gain, severe skin breakouts, and debilitating menstrual cramps that were bad enough to make her sit out PE class. “During the peak of high school, I became incredibly insecure about the weight gain,” Nitha, now 21 years old, recalls. “I stopped taking pictures of myself altogether because I didn’t want to see them posted anywhere. I stopped clicking selfies and didn't want anyone to take my pictures either." “The last time I had an ultrasound and went through a couple of tests, my PMOS symptoms were worse," Nitha says. “The doctors told me then that it would be very difficult for me to have a child in the future. items.title: Two Bengaluru athletes shine at Gay Games, urge support for LGBTQIA+ sportspersons
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Bengaluru’s queer community gathered at 1Shanthiroad Studio/Gallery on Thursday, August 6, to felicitate athletes Gowthami Kandhasami (Goaty) and Sumit Pawar, who represented India at the Gay Games 2026 in València, Spain. The event, titled Celebrating Queer Excellence, was organised by the LGBTQIA+ and sports verticals of the All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC), the Indian National Congress’ professional wing, along with Queer Nilayam and Dark Vibe Society. Goaty won seven medals — four gold and three silver — at the Games. Competing in the 25–29 age category, she won gold in the high jump, the 5 km road race, the 10,000 m indoor run, and the marathon. She also won silver in the 10 km road race, the mixed 4x400 m relay, and the overall women's marathon standings. Sumit won gold in the javelin throw. The felicitation was led by Priyank Sukanand, head of AIPC Karnataka’s LGBTQIA+ vertical, in the presence of writer, art curator, and historian Suresh Jayaram, founder of 1Shanthiroad Studio/Gallery.
